title: Cross-Probe Contrastive Stability Suite and Labeling Contract
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Overview
========

This document defines the Cross-Probe Contrastive Stability Suite (CPCSS): a standardized benchmark and labeling contract used to detect, triage, and quantify subtle fidelity regressions across probe families (priming, few-shot, function-calls, and long-context). CPCSS is intended for evaluators, model-onboarding engineers, and quality guardrails owners who manage shadow-to-canary promotions for mixed-precision and quantized artifacts.

Why this exists
----------------
- Many regressions are only visible when comparing closely related probes (e.g., two priming variants) rather than absolute thresholds.
- Contrastive, cohort-based checks surface small but systematic semantic shifts that break downstream heuristics.
- A labeling contract ensures consistent human annotations and enables automated signal fusion across telemetry, evaluator outputs, and user-facing metrics.

Scope and audience
------------------
- Scope: probe families used in production prompt sets, evaluator-driven shadow traffic, and canary promotion workflows.
- Audience: evaluator team, model-onboarding, applied-ML SREs, product owners of ML-features.

Key definitions
---------------
- Probe: an input variant used to exercise a narrow slice of model behavior (e.g., few-shot prompt for entity extraction).
- Anchor probe: canonical reference input for a slice.
- Contrast pair: (anchor, variant) used to compute a directional delta.
- Stability delta: aggregated metric representing deviation (semantic + token-level) between anchor and variant.

Suite components (high level)
----------------------------
1) Probe catalog: canonicalized probe families, priming lexicon, and minimal postprocessing rules.
2) Contrast scoring: multi-signal score combining semantic similarity, function-call parity, and tokenization drift.
3) Labeling contract: human review guidelines, annotation matrix, and adjudication rules.
4) Triaging playbook: priority matrix, automated bisect suggestions, and rollback gates.

Probe catalog requirements (table)
----------------------------------
| field | example | requirement |
|---|---|---|
| probe_id | priming-weather-v1 | short, unique, hyphenated |
| family | priming | one of: priming, fewshot, functioncall, longcontext |
| seed_inputs | 250 | minimum 200 inputs per probe for statistical power |
| anchor_policy | most-recent-stable | anchors must be pinned to a model version and stored in the probe registry |
| max_context_tokens | 4096 | documented per-probe |

Contrast scoring algorithm (conceptual)
----------------------------------------
- Compute three signals for each (anchor, variant) pair:
  1. Semantic alignment (SA): embedding cosine of normalized outputs (use embedding service: redwood-emb-v1).
  2. Function-call parity (FCP): boolean + weighted token difference for functioncall probes.
  3. Token drift (TD): BPE token divergence normalized by reference length.
- Combined stability delta (SD) = 0.6*SA_delta + 0.3*FCP_penalty + 0.1*TD_score (tunable per-family).
- Thresholding: SD > 0.12 triggers automated triage; SD in [0.08,0.12] creates a medium-priority alert.

Concrete example (command snippets)
----------------------------------
1) Run a local contrast job against shadow cohort:

$ rwd-eval run contrast --probe priming-weather-v1 --anchor-version v2025-11-02 --variant-version staging-quant-v3 --sample 1000 --out results/priming-weather-contrast.json

2) Compute embedding SA (example Python):

from redwood_sdk import EmbeddingsClient
emb = EmbeddingsClient(model='redwood-emb-v1')
anchor_vecs = emb.embed_batch(anchor_texts)
variant_vecs = emb.embed_batch(variant_texts)
# cosine per pair -> SA_delta = 1 - mean(cosine(anchor,variant))

Labeling contract (human annotation)
------------------------------------
Purpose: produce consistent human labels for contrast cases where automated signals are ambiguous.

1) Triage classes (single-label per example):
   - NO_REGRESSION: outputs are functionally equivalent for the use-case.
   - MINOR_QUALITY_CHANGE: cosmetic or brevity-related differences not affecting downstream decisions.
   - FUNCTIONAL_REGRESSION: meaningful change that alters correctness or safety.
   - BEHAVIORAL_DRIFT: change in tone/persona or contextual hallucination risk.

2) Annotation guidelines (bullet form):
   - Annotators must read both outputs in context and assume the downstream consumer is a "structured ingestor" (e.g., extraction pipeline).
   - If function-call probes differ in arguments or call/no-call, label FUNCTIONAL_REGRESSION.
   - For multi-turn longcontext probes, check memory consistency for the last 3 turns.

3) Adjudication flow: 3-annotator consensus with majority label; if all three disagree, route to SME for adjudication and add to gold set.

Label schema (CSV columns)
--------------------------
| probe_id | input_id | anchor_output | variant_output | label | annotator | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| priming-weather-v1 | 000124 | {...} | {...} | FUNCTIONAL_REGRESSION | alice | changed date parsing |

Quality gates and rollout integration
-------------------------------------
- Canary promotion block: any probe family with SD > 0.12 and label ratio (FUNCTIONAL_REGRESSION) > 1% for samples >= 500 blocks rollout.
- Auto-fallback: if rollout proceeds and live telemetry (user-error-rate) increases by 20% vs baseline within first 6 hours, trigger automatic fallback to previous model.
- Canary sampling: 0.5% live traffic min, stratified across tenant cohorts for at least 24 hours before scale-up.

Monitoring and SLOs
-------------------
- Probe stability SLO: 99.5% of contrast pairs must have SD <= 0.08 in promotion windows.
- Annotation latency SLO: 90% of queued contrast samples labeled within 48 hours for priority alerts.
- Telemetry drift SLO: deploys must show <15% relative increase in user-facing error signals (extraction failures, function-call mis-invocations) for 72-hour evaluation window.

Automated triage playbook (numbered steps)
------------------------------------------
1. Run contrast job against staged model with the full probe catalog (CI hook).
2. If any family reports SD > 0.12, auto-open a regression ticket in JIRA with priority P1-P2 depending on impact.
3. Attach 500 randomly sampled contrast pairs to the ticket and kick off labeling (auto-assign rounds).
4. If labeled FUNCTIONAL_REGRESSION ratio > 1% -> block canary and assign to model-onboarding owner.
5. If labeled MINOR_QUALITY_CHANGE -> schedule follow-up evaluation with increased sample size and localized prompt rewrite experiment.
6. Once triage completes, produce a regression summary and recommend: rollback / hotfix prompt patch / accept with mitigation.

Ownership and escalation
------------------------
- Probe library steward: Applied ML Evaluations (owner: Maya Thompson) — maintains catalog and priming lexicon.
- Onboarding owner: Model Onboarding team — responsible for promotions, canary config, and rollback.
- SRE escalation: Eng SRE oncall for inference platform for automated fallback and capacity anomalies.

Runbook snippets (when a canary is blocked)
-------------------------------------------
1) Immediate steps (first 30 minutes):
   - Pager: paging list (model-onboarding@redwood.com, eng-sre-oncall).
   - Snapshot: capture probe contrast results, top-20 worst SD pairs, and telemetry spike facets.
   - If customers impacted (per tenant sampling), open a customer incident page and notify CS.

2) For solving regression:
   - Try prompt mitigation: local prompt rewrite and re-run contrast subset (target top 50 failure pairs).
   - If mitigation fails, revert model and initiate postmortem with regression impact index (see related: /applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/regression-impact-index-and-prioritization-framework-2024).

Metric and artifact retention
----------------------------
- Contrast results and label artifacts are stored in the probe-registry S3 bucket with path: s3://probe-registry/{probe_id}/contrast/{date}/results.json (retain 365 days).
- Gold adjudicated samples are appended to the goldset DB (redwood-eval-gold.v1) and retained indefinitely.

Privacy and annotation safety
----------------------------
- Remove PII prior to human labeling using the pii-sanitizer pipeline (cli: rwd-sanitize --redact).
- Annotators sign the evaluator NDA and label in the secure annotator environment (no external downloads).

Appendix A — Example scoring weights by family
----------------------------------------------
| family | SA_weight | FCP_weight | TD_weight | block_threshold |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| priming | 0.7 | 0.2 | 0.1 | 0.14 |
| fewshot | 0.6 | 0.25 | 0.15 | 0.12 |
| functioncall | 0.4 | 0.5 | 0.1 | 0.10 |
| longcontext | 0.65 | 0.2 | 0.15 | 0.13 |
